advanced.title: Advanced connection settings
advanced.description: Only needed for plants that do not use the standard Climatix credentials/PIN. Leave the defaults unless your controller was reconfigured. With custom credentials, a changed IP address is only picked up from Home Assistant's DHCP data; the network is never searched with them.

manual.title: Ochsner heat pump (local)
manual.description: Enter your heat pump IP address or hostname. Once identified by serial number, address changes are recovered automatically.

discovery_confirm.title: {model}
discovery_confirm.description: Found **{model}** at **{host}** (serial **{serial}**). Confirm to add this heat pump.

reconfigure.title: Change heat pump address
reconfigure.description: Enter the heat pump's current IP address or hostname. The serial number must match the configured heat pump; the saved credentials and PIN are kept.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach a Climatix controller at this IP (check the address and that the device is on your network).
error.auth_failed: The controller rejected the standard credentials. Use the advanced settings to enter your controller's username/password.
error.probe_failed: Connected, but no catalog datapoint was readable. This usually means a non-default PIN — use the advanced settings to enter it.
error.identity_changed: A different controller now responds at this address. Run discovery again.
error.serial_mismatch: The heat pump at this address has a different serial number than the configured one.

abort.no_devices_found: No heat pumps found. Check Home Assistant’s network selection or enter the address manually.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The heat pump address was updated.

progress.scan_network: Searching the local network for heat pumps. This can take a few minutes.

init.title: Options
init.description: Gated polling default threshold is 20. You can increase it if you see connection errors.

data.language: Language of entity names and labels
data.local_scan_now: Local catalog scan now (accountless; add missing entities)
data.redownload_bundle: Re-download bundle from OTS (add missing entities)
data.configure_entities: Configure sensor/number device class and unit

entity_override_select.title: Entity overrides
entity_override_select.description: Select an entity to override its device class and unit.

entity_override_edit.title: Edit entity override
entity_override_edit.description: Set overrides for the selected entity. Leave fields empty to keep defaults.

error.invalid_scan_interval: Please enter a polling interval of at least 1 second.
error.invalid_polling_threshold: Please enter a gated polling threshold between 10 and 120.
error.invalid_max_ids: Please enter a max values-per-request between 1 and 200.
error.invalid_range: Maximum must be greater than minimum.
error.no_entities: The downloaded bundle produced no entities; nothing was changed.
error.no_controllers: This entry has no controllers to update.
error.no_bundle_key: No stored bundle key found for this controller.
error.no_ots_ids: The OTS config/site id is missing for this controller.

address_unknown.title: {name} cannot be found
address_unknown.description:
**{name}** is not answering at **{host}**, and Home Assistant's DHCP data shows no other address for it. Because it uses custom credentials, the integration does not search the network for it, so they are never sent to other devices.

If the heat pump's IP address changed, go to **Settings → Devices & services → Ochsner Local OTS**, choose **Reconfigure** from the entry's menu and enter the new address. If the heat pump was only switched off, this message disappears once it answers again.
